take_homes: The measure must not move while you measure. The judge file is hashed and checked, so a number that comes from the loop can be defended.
A flat or zero score may mean the checker is blind. Test the judge against a handful of human-scored outputs once before trusting it.
Decide per category whether an agent drafts, gets reviewed first, or sends on its own, and keep reading real outputs myself.

monday.move: Ask my controller to try the month-end variance commentary with an agent, with a judge that checks every figure against the ledger, and compare the result with the last close.
monday.when: Month-end close, if IT clears the tool for finance data
monday.stop_condition: The judge passes a figure that differs from the ledger, or the cost per close is not below the hours it saves
monday.blocker: IT has not approved the tool for finance data, and nobody has given me a cost per month for 40 people.

misconception.why: The module says the work gets better because people write down what good means and keep a fixed judge. That is a capability the organisation builds, not a licence. It still never says what it costs, so I only half believe it.

one_line: Good control idea: a fixed judge, checked against people, with the hash to prove it. Not one number on cost or payback in forty-five minutes, so I'm not sure what I'd tell the board.
